summary: Iteration 15 - /api/reels video playback/download fix. Backend: 17/17 pytest cases pass against the public URL. Range: bytes=0-1 → 206 'bytes 0-1/1813264'; bytes=1000000- → 206 with correct Content-Range and length; bytes=-500 → 206 last 500 bytes; bytes=99999999- → 416 with 'Content-Range: bytes */1813264'; no Range → 200 full file. Concatenated chunked ranges md5 == full-file md5. ?download=1 sets Content-Disposition: attachment on both the mp4 and the cover jpg. Traversal: ..%2Fserver.py → 404; %2e%2e → safe 307 to /api/reels (never reads server.py). Regression: /api/static/logos/logo_dark_transparent.png, /api/try, /api/presentation all 200. Frontend: /api/reels at iPhone viewport (390x844) renders with correct heading, large tappable 'Download video' and 'Download cover image' buttons (>44px). <video> has playsinline, controls, preload=metadata, correct poster + src. From the real browser, the server returned 206 video/mp4 for the mp4 and 200 image/jpeg for the poster. Clicking both download buttons triggered real downloads with the right filenames and 0 main-frame navigations (confirming no reload loop like the user reported). In-browser timed-playback assertion was skipped because this environment's headless Chromium shell lacks the H.264 codec that iOS Safari ships natively; the file is standard AVC/MP4 (ftyp isom/iso2/mp41, avc1) so iOS Safari will decode it, and all Range semantics required for mid-stream seeking are proven at the HTTP level.
critical_code_review_comments: reels.py reads the full file into memory via p.read_bytes() for 200 responses. The current reel is 1.8 MB so it's fine, but if larger reels are ever added, switch to FileResponse or a streaming iterator to avoid loading the entire file per request.

The %2e%2e path is handled safely (307 to /api/reels listing, a public page) by Starlette's URL normalisation rather than the _file() guard. Not a vulnerability but worth noting that defence-in-depth works.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The sandbox's bundled Chromium (/pw-browsers/chromium_headless_shell-1208) does not include the proprietary H.264 codec, so in-browser <video>.play() on the reel throws NotSupportedError. Do NOT treat that as a product bug. Prove playback correctness via HTTP-level Range tests (see test_reels.py) and the fact that the browser's own metadata fetch returns 206 video/mp4. iOS Safari and desktop Chrome with codecs will play the file.
rca_of_issue: Original user bug (iPhone reload loop, 'plays a couple seconds', can't long-press to save) was caused by Starlette's StaticFiles ignoring HTTP Range and always returning 200. iOS Safari's media engine needs 206 Partial Content with a correct Content-Range to seek inside an MP4; it treats a 200 to a Range request as 'source failed', aborts, and reloads/restarts, which looks like the page refreshing and only playing the first few seconds. The fix adds /api/reels/file/{name} that parses the Range header (both explicit 'bytes=start-end' and suffix 'bytes=-N'), emits Accept-Ranges: bytes, returns 206 with Content-Range for valid ranges, 416 when out of range, and 200 when no Range is sent. ?download=1 adds Content-Disposition: attachment so the long-press/download gesture produces a saveable file. All verified end-to-end against the public URL.
